additions.text: On the pocket radio, Lola talks to a listener. Her name is Salomé and she is a nurse.
Good morning. This is Radio Kilómetro Cero. Who is calling?
Hi, Lola. I am Salomé. I am a nurse. I am from Colombia.
I am at home. I have water and bread. I am fine.
What does Salomé have at home?
What do you have at home to eat?
Do you listen to the radio?
Alex is a delivery rider. He is on the Gran Vía and calls his sister Camila.
Hi, Camila. I am on the Gran Vía.
Yes. But there is a red bus on the ground. And there is a green cloud.
OK. I am going on my bike. Ten minutes.
How many minutes does Alex need?
Do you have brothers or sisters?
How do you go to work?
In the shelter, Andrea helps with the water. She talks to an old man, Ramón.
Hello, sir. What is your name?
My name is Ramón. I am seventy years old.
Here is a bottle of water, Ramón.
Thank you! Are you from here?
No, I am from Ecuador. I live in Madrid.
What is your name and how old are you?
Do you drink a lot of water?
In the metro, a musician from Cuba plays the guitar. A girl, Ximena, talks to him.
Hi. I am Manuel. I play the guitar here, in the metro.
How nice! Do you play every day?
Yes. Music is good for fear.
That is true. Now I am calmer.
What do you do when you are afraid?
The radio finds an audio from the lab. Doctor Elena talks to Javier, her assistant.
Close the door. Call the boss.
Do you have a boss? What is he or she like?
What do you do if something is broken?
Lola talks to Emilio, a DJ from the Dominican Republic who lives in Malasaña.
Emilio, what is happening in Malasaña?
There is music in the square. There are coloured lights.
People dance. They are happy. Tonight, merengue.
What do you do at night?
Is there a nice square in your city?
In Atocha, a mother from Uruguay talks to Álvaro, a train driver.
Excuse me, what time does the train leave?
It leaves at eleven forty. It goes to Valencia.
I have two children. Is there room?
I do not know. There are six hundred seats.
What time does the train leave?
How many children does Valentina have?
What time do you leave home?
Do you like travelling by train?
The radio finds a military frequency. A sergeant talks to Mario, a soldier from Paraguay.
Yes, sergeant. I am at the palace gate.
Yes, there is a family. They are cold.
Is there a palace in your city?
What do you like more: the cold or the heat?
Yuleisy is a nurse. She sends a voice message to her brother Sebastián, in Caracas.
Hi, Sebastián. I am at the hospital. I work a lot.
Yes, yes. A coffee and a sandwich.
That is not eating well. A kiss. Mum loves you.
What do you eat at midday?
Lola talks to Jaime, the boatman. The boat leaves the river at dawn.
Jaime, are you at the river?
Yes, Lola. The boat is ready.
At seven. When the sun comes up.
What time does the boat leave?
What does Lola say at the end?
What time do you get up?
Is there a river in your city?
Do you like going by boat?
…this is Radio Kilometre Zero, broadcasting from somewhere in Madrid…
The government asks for calm. The roads out of the city are closed…
Don’t breathe the green cloud. I repeat: don’t breathe…
If anyone can hear me… the lab in the Retiro… can you hear me?…
Puerta del Sol. It is six in the morning. There is a table, a microphone and a woman. Her name is Lola.
Hi! I am Lola. I talk on the radio.
Hi, Lola. I have a vaccine.
A vaccine? Great! Madrid is in danger. There is a virus.
From the Retiro, I think. It is a big park. Take this radio. It is small.
Lola says: “It is a big park.”
Do you listen to the radio?
What time do you get up?
Next to the bear, there is a kiosk. An old man is inside. His name is Paco.
Yes. My wife is not here. I am alone at home. I am better here.
A little. Look, a number for you: six. It is for luck.
Paco says: “a number for you: six.”
Gran Vía. There is a broken bus in the street. A driver is sitting. His name is Julián.
Hello. It is my bus. I am a driver.
Yes, I am fine. The passengers are fine too. There are eleven.
But there are army trucks in the street. They go to the Retiro. It is strange.
Do you go to work by bus?
On top of a car, there is a girl with a phone. Her name is Vera. She talks to a lot of people online.
Hi, guys! Today I am on the Gran Vía. Look!
Hi. Who are you talking to?
With my followers. I have two million. Do you have a vaccine?
I take garlic and lemon. It is better!
No, Vera. Garlic is not a medicine.
How many followers does Vera have?
Do you use your phone a lot?
Which social networks do you use?
Plaza Mayor. It is a shelter. There is a table at the gate. A police officer is at the table. Her name is Montse.
Hello. I have the vaccine. Look, the green shield.
OK. Come in. Inside there are three hundred people. There are many children.
And you? Do you have family?
Yes, a brother. He is outside, in a tent. The rules are for everyone.
Montse says: “He is outside, in a tent.”
Do you have brothers or sisters?
How many people are there in your family?
In a blue tent there is a board and twelve children. The teacher’s name is Carmen. She has glasses.
Good morning. This is my class.
Hi, kids! Is there class every day?
Yes. From ten to one. We read, we write and we count.
Yes, they like it a lot. Here they are not afraid.
What time does the class start?
What is your favourite teacher’s name?
Chamberí metro station. On the platform there is a blanket and a torch. There is a girl and a boy: Sara and Toni.
Hi. We have been here for five days.
Not really. Sara is angry with me.
Yes. Toni writes to his ex-girlfriend. I do not like it!
I want to go out to the street. Sara wants to stay here.
Talk, please. You are a couple.
Because Toni writes to his ex-girlfriend.
Sara says: “Toni writes to his ex-girlfriend. I do not like it!”
Do you have a partner or are you single?
What do you do when you are angry?
At the end of the platform, there is an old man in a blue uniform. His name is Emilio. He is very kind.
Hello, young one. I am Emilio. I know the metro well: it is my home.
I want to go to the Retiro. Is there a way?
Yes. There is an old tunnel. It is safe.
Look, here you have a map. First, to the right. Then, straight on.
Thank you very much, Don Emilio.
Emilio says: “There is an old tunnel. It is safe.”
Is there a metro in your city?
Retiro Park. In the Crystal Palace there is a lab. There are green tanks. A doctor waits at the door.
Hello. I am Elena. I am a doctor.
Yes. It is an accident. A tank is broken.
The vaccine is mine. Take this notebook. It is the formula. It is very important.
OK. I am going to the hospital with the notebook.
Elena says: “Take this notebook. It is the formula.”
Do you go to the doctor often?
Next to the lake in the Retiro, a man has a camera. His name is Marcos. He is from Mexico.
Hello. I am a journalist. I am from Mexico.
What are you doing in Madrid?
I am making a report about the virus. I have videos of the army trucks.
Yes, a lot. But now the city is empty and sad.
Do you like taking photos or videos?
Malasaña, at night. There are coloured lights and music. A bar is open. The waiter’s name is Nacho.
Hi! Welcome. Do you want a vermouth? It is free.
Here you are. Look, there are some boxes in the bar. They are not mine.
Green bottles. There is a name: Salvatierra.
What does the mascot want to drink?
What do you drink in the morning?
Do you like going out at night?
On the other side of the square there is a restaurant. A cook gives food to the neighbours. His name is Arturo. He is from Argentina.
Hi! Are you hungry? There are lentils.
Yes, thanks. How much is it?
Nothing. It is free for everyone.
Very kind! Do you have family?
Yes, a daughter. She is in Valencia. I have no news from her.
Do you cook at home every day?
Atocha station. There are many people with suitcases. There is a train. Only one. A woman in uniform speaks.
Hello. I am Mercedes. I am the head of the station.
To Valencia. It leaves tonight. There are six hundred seats.
And how many people are here?
Two thousand! It is a very big problem.
Mercedes says: “To Valencia. It leaves tonight.”
Do you like travelling by train?
Which city do you want to visit?
In a room in Atocha, a man in a suit sells green bottles. His name is Íñigo. There are many rich people.
Hello. One dose costs five thousand euros.
That is the price. People want to live.
How much does one dose cost?
Íñigo says: “One dose costs five thousand euros.”
What things are expensive in your city?
Do you buy a lot online?
Royal Palace. There are many soldiers. In a big room, a man eats biscuits. His name is Gonzalo. He works for the Government.
I have a question. Does the Government know the truth?
Yes. We know everything. But it is a secret.
Because people are afraid. It is difficult.
A man eats biscuits in a big room.
Do you always tell the truth?
What do you eat when you are nervous?
In the palace courtyard there is a helicopter. A woman with a helmet looks at a map. She is Captain Inés.
Stop! Ah, you have the shield. You are fine.
I need to go to the hospital.
Take this paper. With it you can pass.
Thank you, captain. Are you in the army?
Yes. I like helping people. It is my job.
In the palace courtyard there is a helicopter.
What do you do in your job?
Field hospital. There are white tents and many beds. A doctor drinks a coffee. Her name is Pilar. She is very tired.
Hello. I am tired. I do not sleep.
I have the formula of the vaccine.
Really? Great! It is good news.
Can you make the vaccine here?
No. I do not have a lab. I make a copy. You take the notebook out of Madrid.
Pilar says: “I am tired. I do not sleep.”
How many hours do you sleep?
Do you drink coffee or tea?
At the hospital door, a nurse puts on coloured wristbands. Her name is Yuleisy. She is from Venezuela.
Hi. Red: you go in now. Green: you wait.
Do you have family in Madrid?
No. My mum is in Caracas. I talk to her every night.
What does the colour red mean?
Yuleisy says: “Red: you go in now.”
Do you talk to your family every day?
Madrid Río. It is seven in the morning. A very old lady waters some flowers at the door of her house.
Good morning. I am Remedios. I am eighty-nine years old.
Hello, madam. Do you live here alone?
Yes. This is my house. I do not want to go anywhere else.
My granddaughter lives in Toledo. Please, take this letter.
Yes, of course. I take the letter.
Remedios says: “My granddaughter lives in Toledo.”
Do you have grandparents? What are their names?
Do you like flowers or plants?
On the river there is an orange boat. A man with a beard is waiting. His name is Jaime. The boat leaves in ten minutes.
Hi! Do you have the formula? Get in the boat.
Yes, here it is. Who else is coming?
A family with a little girl. The boat is small.
Out of Madrid. Let’s go! It is already daytime.
On the river there is an orange boat.
Do you like the water: the river or the sea?
What do you do at weekends?
